name: pdk-soketi-cluster-presence-webhooks
instr:
We need Soketi clusters to keep customer billing and presence UIs consistent when subscriptions arrive on several servers. Extend the Redis adapter, channel subscription flow and webhook delivery so membership and lifecycle notifications describe the whole cluster rather than any one process.

A channel's transition from zero subscribers to one or more produces exactly one `channel_occupied`; its return to zero produces exactly one `channel_vacated`, including when twenty connections join concurrently on three instances. For presence channels, a user with concurrent connections on different instances produces one `member_added` and, after the last connection leaves, one `member_removed`. A killed instance's only subscribers disappear from the cluster within 10 seconds, with one removal and one vacancy notification. Following churn, `pusher_internal:subscription_succeeded` reports the same live presence members on every instance. Webhook receivers see lifecycle and membership transitions in their per-channel order: on a presence channel, `channel_occupied` precedes `member_added`, and the final `member_removed` precedes `channel_vacated`. This includes ten rapid occupy/vacate cycles sent through the SQS FIFO driver; identical successive events must not be deduplicated away. For SQS FIFO, group every lifecycle event type for the same app and channel together, and use a different group for a different channel so its ordering is independent.
